Lando Norris secured his and McLaren's first win of the 2026 season with a brilliant drive at the Hungarian Grand Prix, bouncing back from an early race scare to dominate the field.

Norris started on pole, but teammate Oscar Piastri snatched the lead with a clever cut-back move at Turn 2 on the opening lap. The two McLarens ran first and second for much of the first half, engaging in a tense intra-team battle while managing tire strategies.

The race flipped completely after the midway point. While navigating blue flags in traffic, Piastri collided with Carlos Sainz at Turn 2, heavily damaging his momentum. Capitalizing on superior clean-air pace and longer stints, Norris surged ahead to claim a net lead. Piastri's afternoon ended in total heartbreak shortly after when a sudden gearbox failure forced him to retire.

A late Virtual Safety Car triggered a flurry of pit activity. Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli seized the opportunity by staying out, securing second and third places respectively.

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton initially crossed the line ahead of Antonelli, but a late five-second penalty for pit-lane speeding dropped him behind teammate Charles Leclerc to fifth. George Russell completed an impressive recovery drive to finish seventh after a disastrous anti-stall start dropped him all the way to 21st.

Meanwhile, Isack Hadjar finished sixth for Red Bull, and Liam Lawson grabbed eighth ahead of Nico Hulkenberg and Arvid Lindblad, who rounded out the points. Aside from Piastri, Cadillac endured a rough day with both Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez retiring due to mechanical issues.

Norris crossed the finish line 15 seconds clear of Verstappen, celebrating a sensational victory before Formula 1 heads into its summer break ahead of the Dutch Grand Prix.

TAMIL NADU SPORTS BUDGET JUMPS 84% WITH THE NEW ELECTION CYCLE

Tamil Nadu's sports allocation has just seen its sharpest jump in years, and the numbers tell a story that goes well beyond rupees; they mark a genuine changing of the guard in state politics. For 2025-26, under the outgoing DMK government led by M.K. Stalin, the Youth Welfare and Sports Development Department under Mr. Siva V. Meyyanathan was allocated roughly ₹572 crore. In February 2026, ahead of the Assembly elections, that same government presented an interim "vote-on-account" budget that bumped the figure to ₹718 crore a modest pre-election increase. Then came the real shift. Tamil Nadu went to the polls in 2026, and a TVK-led coalition took charge. On August 5, 2026, the new government's Finance Minister, Dr. N. Marie Wilson, presented the state's first full "revised" budget, raising sports under Mr. Aadhav Arjuna's ministry spent ₹1,051 crore. That's about 84% higher than the 2025-26 figure, and roughly 46% above even the outgoing government's own interim estimate for the same year. The flagship new initiative is a set of 10 Olympic Centres of Excellence across the state, aimed explicitly at producing Olympic gold medallists though the exact per-centre funding figure has varied across reports, with the minister's own remarks putting the initial allocation in the single-digit crores and later coverage citing a larger figure near ₹50 crore for the full initiative. Locations and sporting disciplines are yet to be announced. Beyond that, ₹42 crore has been set aside for the Tamil Nadu Rural Games, an initiative to widen grassroots participation outside urban centres and ₹22 crore has been earmarked as financial assistance for 500 athletes. Schools also feature prominently, with a push toward guaranteed daily sports time as part of the broader plan. Big first budgets from new governments are rarely just accounting exercises; they're statements of priority. By nearly doubling sports funding in its maiden budget, the TVK-led coalition appears to be signalling that youth engagement and sporting infrastructure will be a visible marker of its governance, distinct from the welfare-pension-and-subsidy model that defined the DMK years. Whether the money translates into functioning Olympic centres and a genuine grassroots pipeline rather than announcements without follow-through, a familiar pattern in Tamil Nadu budgets will be the real test in the years ahead.
